title: Circle of Competence
coreMove: Mark the edge of earned competence before deciding where to play, learn, or defer.
sourcePressure: The source says the size of the circle matters less than knowing the perimeter. It uses Rose Blumkin, Charlie Munger, and the chess grandmaster example to show that advantage does not automatically transfer to adjacent domains.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The weak version says stay in your comfort zone or avoid hard unfamiliar learning.

sourceAnchors.name: Rose Blumkin
sourceAnchors.detail: the source uses her focused knowledge of furniture, cash, and real estate, contrasted with not knowing stocks, as an anchor for staying around spots of competence
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Rose Blumkin's edge was not a halo around every business problem; it was furniture, cash, leases, and the ground she knew by touch.

sourceAnchors.name: Charlie Munger
sourceAnchors.detail: the source uses him as the practical voice for playing where you have an edge and avoiding games others understand better
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Munger's warning is blunt: the other table may look open, but it belongs to people who have paid for knowledge you are only borrowing.

sourceAnchors.name: a chess grandmaster
sourceAnchors.detail: the source uses a chess grandmaster example to show that excellence in one domain does not generalize automatically
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The grandmaster can see sixty-four squares clearly and still be a beginner when the board changes.

hook: circle drawn on whiteboard as whole scene
tryThisNow: write what you are good at

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person 'You' direct address, retrospective 'It took her three weeks to see', question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

exampleSpecs.audience: a shop owner who knows aging, suppliers, and local customers but is tempted by online meal kits
exampleSpecs.stakes: a profitable shop could burn cash in a business whose logistics she has not earned
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Andrew places the aged-cheese margin sheet beside the refrigerated meal-kit shipping quote and marks which facts come from direct experience and which are guesses
exampleSpecs.firstImage: the ammoniac bite of washed-rind cheese in the prep room

exampleSpecs.audience: a senior nurse asked to interpret a scan outside her certification
exampleSpecs.stakes: a fast call could mislead treatment before radiology arrives
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Sophie names exactly what she can verify from the bedside protocol and exactly where the radiologist's edge begins
exampleSpecs.firstImage: blue gel drying around the ultrasound probe

exampleSpecs.domain: chess club coach asked about poker
exampleSpecs.audience: a brilliant chess coach invited into a high-stakes poker stream
exampleSpecs.stakes: his pattern skill may be mistaken for transferable edge
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Nicolas reviews one poker hand aloud, catches himself using chess certainty, and writes 'learn' rather than 'play' beside the invitation
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a paused river card glowing on a laptop beside a wooden chess clock

exampleSpecs.audience: a warehouse operator deciding whether to buy a neighboring building
exampleSpecs.stakes: one familiar lease term hides an unfamiliar zoning fight
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Mikkel circles the parts of the deal his warehouse history covers, then slides the zoning packet to counsel instead of pretending the whole transaction is inside his circle
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a folded zoning packet under a tape measure on a loading dock

exampleSpecs.audience: a filmmaker who understands editing but not international licensing
exampleSpecs.stakes: a rights clause could lock the film away from festivals for years
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: You watch Layla highlight every clause she can explain unaided and every clause that requires a distribution lawyer before the signature page moves
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a festival lanyard lying across a redlined rights contract

exampleSpecs.audience: a mountain guide strong on route feel but new to a different snowpack
exampleSpecs.stakes: local confidence could outrun unfamiliar avalanche patterns
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Janek writes the day's route plan only after asking the local forecaster where his home-range knowledge stops applying
exampleSpecs.firstImage: wind-slab crystals skittering across a tailgate map

skillTargets: identify the perimeter of earned knowledge
distinguish learning outside the circle from pretending
decide when to defer to a better edge

tryThisNowSpec: Choose one live decision. Draw three boxes labeled play, learn, and defer, then put each part of the decision where your evidence says it belongs.

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm - a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'
